question: If $B=\begin{bmatrix}1&-5\\ 0&-3\end{bmatrix}$ and $A+2B=\begin{bmatrix}0&4\\ -7&5\end{bmatrix}$, find the matrix $A$.
explanation:
**Step 1:** Given $A + 2B = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 \\ -7 & 5\end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 \\ 0 & -3\end{bmatrix}$.

**Step 2:** Compute $2B$:
$2B = 2 \begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 \\ 0 & -3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -10 \\ 0 & -6\end{bmatrix}$.

**Step 3:** Substitute into the equation:
$A + \begin{bmatrix}2 & -10 \\ 0 & -6\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 \\ -7 & 5\end{bmatrix}$.

**Step 4:** Solve for $A$:
$A = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 \\ -7 & 5\end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix}2 & -10 \\ 0 & -6\end{bmatrix}$.

**Step 5:** Subtract element-wise:
$A = \begin{bmatrix}0-2 & 4-(-10) \\ -7-0 & 5-(-6)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 14 \\ -7 & 11\end{bmatrix}$.

**Answer:** $A = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 14 \\ -7 & 11\end{bmatrix}$
